record.title: Bird flu at Nobeoka layer farm, season's 13th outbreak
record.detail: MAFF confirmed highly pathogenic avian influenza at a farm of about 6,000 egg-laying hens in Nobeoka; all birds were being culled, with movement limits within 3 km and shipping limits to 10 km. Nearly 3.9 million chickens had been culled across the season's 13 outbreaks.
record.agency: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries
record.attribution: Per Xinhua, citing Japan's agriculture ministry

record.title: North Korea fires two ballistic missiles into Sea of Japan
record.detail: MOD said North Korea launched at least two ballistic missiles from its west coast around 7:54 and 08:05, flying about 900–950 km at ~50 km altitude on possibly irregular trajectories and falling outside Japan's EEZ; Japan protested via its Beijing embassy.

record.title: NPA plans tougher laws on account trading and 'remittance side jobs'
record.detail: The NPA said it would seek tougher penalties for illegally transferring bank accounts, regulate 'remittance side jobs', and let police open fictitiously named accounts to trace proceeds; 4,362 account-trading cases were handled in 2024.
record.attribution: Jiji Press via Nippon.com citing NPA

record.title: 13 returned from Bavet, Cambodia fraud base arrested
record.detail: Tokyo MPD and Kanagawa police arrested 13 Japanese aged 20s–60s who had been detained in Bavet, Cambodia in November 2025, over fake-police phone scams including about ¥11 million taken from a Kanagawa woman in her 60s.
record.agency: Metropolitan Police Department; Kanagawa Prefectural Police
record.attribution: Jiji Press via Nippon.com citing police

record.title: Power fault at Tamachi halts Yamanote and Keihin-Tohoku lines
record.detail: Power failed to come back after overnight maintenance near Tamachi Station, with smoke seen from a track-side equipment box; JR East's Yamanote and Keihin-Tohoku lines were disrupted for up to nine hours, affecting about 673,000 passengers.

record.title: Russian Tu-95 bomber groups probe Sea of Japan
record.detail: Three groups of Russian Tu-95 bombers, some escorted by Su-35S/Su-30SM fighters, flew over the Sea of Japan, turning off Shimane and the Noto Peninsula and west of Hokkaido; JASDF scrambled, and Defense Minister Koizumi called it a show of force. An IL-20 ELINT flight followed on Jan. 23.
record.attribution: USNI News citing Japan Joint Staff Office and Defense Minister Koizumi

record.title: Record snow along Sea of Japan coast kills at least 30
record.detail: Heavy snow from January 20 killed 30 people and injured 290, mostly in Niigata (12) and Akita (6); Aomori City reached 183 cm in places, beating a 1986 record. The prime minister ordered an SDF deployment for relief.
record.place: Sea of Japan coast (Aomori, Niigata, Akita, Hokkaido)
record.agency: Fire and Disaster Management Agency; Japan Meteorological Agency
record.attribution: Casualty figures per FDMA and NHK as reported by Al Jazeera

record.title: Norovirus-type gastroenteritis rises for fifth straight week
record.detail: JIHS sentinel data showed infectious gastroenteritis at 9.48 patients per clinic in the week to February 8, a fifth weekly rise; norovirus food poisoning closed a hotel in Aomori (47 ill) and a restaurant in Nara (10 ill).
record.attribution: Surveillance figures per JIHS as reported by CGTN (Chinese state media)

record.title: Fisheries Agency seizes Chinese fishing boat off Nagasaki
record.detail: The Fisheries Agency seized a Chinese fishing boat with 11 aboard about 165 km SSW of Meshima in Japan's EEZ and arrested the captain for allegedly evading an onboard inspection; first such seizure of a Chinese boat since 2022, per reports.
record.attribution: Al Jazeera citing Japan Fisheries Agency

record.title: Special fraud losses near-double to ¥142.3bn in 2025
record.detail: NPA figures show special fraud (tokushu sagi) losses of ¥142.3 billion in 2025 from 27,832 cases; fake-police scams more than doubled to 11,014 cases and ¥100.5 billion, and social-media investment/romance fraud rose 48.2% to 15,168 cases and ¥183.4 billion.
record.attribution: Nippon.com citing National Police Agency 2025 statistics; page undated, date set to NPA's annual release (Feb 12, 2026, per Japan Times URL, not opened)

record.title: Five killed in fire at Shimonoseki temple
record.detail: Fire broke out around 02:30 at a two-storey wooden temple with attached living quarters, killing five residents and destroying three structures including the main hall; police and fire officials are investigating the cause.
record.attribution: Per Xinhua, citing NHK and Kyodo

record.title: Bird flu at Abira chicken farm, about 190,000 birds to be culled
record.detail: MAFF confirmed highly pathogenic avian influenza at a chicken farm in Abira, Hokkaido, Japan's 21st outbreak of the season and Hokkaido's fourth; all about 190,000 chickens were to be culled.
record.agency: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries
record.attribution: Per Xinhua, citing Japan's agriculture ministry; republished by GlobalSecurity.org

record.title: North Korea salvo of about 10 short-range missiles
record.detail: North Korea fired about 10 KN-25 rocket-launcher ballistic missiles from Sunan; Japan estimated a max altitude of 80 km and range of about 340 km, landing outside Japan's EEZ, and MOD called the launches a violation of UN resolutions.
record.attribution: USNI News citing Japan MOD and South Korea JCS

record.title: Six killed in truck pile-up in Nonobori Tunnel, Shin-Meishin Expressway
record.detail: Around 02:20 a large truck rear-ended vehicles queued for roadworks in the southbound Nonobori Tunnel in Mie; six people including three children died and vehicles caught fire. The driver was later arrested on a negligent-driving-causing-death charge and reportedly told police she was looking at her smartphone.
record.attribution: Per Yomiuri Shimbun/ANN; driver's statement as reported by police sources

record.title: Norovirus in school-lunch bread sickens 633 in Kumatori
record.detail: 633 students and staff at eight elementary and junior high schools fell ill; the public health centre blamed norovirus in bread served in school lunches and suspended the bread maker for five days.

record.title: FSA revises AML/CFT guidelines for financial institutions
record.detail: The Financial Services Agency published revised Guidelines for Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism and updated FAQs to strengthen financial institutions' AML/CFT frameworks.

record.title: Cabinet approves harsher penalties for selling bank accounts
record.detail: The Takaichi cabinet approved a bill raising the penalty for selling accounts to up to three years' prison or a ¥5 million fine (five years/¥10 million for habitual sellers), penalising unauthorised 'remittance side jobs' and allowing police-run fictitious accounts.

record.title: Measles cases hit 236, above any year since 2020 for the period
record.detail: JIHS counted 236 measles cases in weeks 1-14, rising to 28-34 a week from week 11; Tokyo had 72, Kagoshima 27, Aichi 23. 30 cases were infected abroad, 12 of them in Indonesia.
record.attribution: Surveillance report by JIHS (as at April 8, 2026)

record.title: 13 men from Bogor, Indonesia scam base arrested in Japan
record.detail: Police arrested 13 Japanese men in their 20s–50s transferred from Indonesia, where they allegedly ran a fake-police scam base in Bogor, West Java, and induced a woman in her 60s to buy and send ¥8 million in ether.
record.attribution: Jiji Press via Nippon.com citing police

record.title: M7.7 quake off Sanriku triggers tsunami warning
record.detail: A preliminary magnitude 7.7 quake (JMA) struck off the Sanriku coast at about 16:52 at 19 km depth, with a 0.8 m tsunami recorded at Kuji; PM Takaichi urged coastal residents to evacuate and nuclear plants reported no abnormalities.
record.attribution: Global Times citing JMA; Kuji coordinates are for the tsunami observation point

record.title: Shell detonates inside Type-10 tank turret at Hijudai; 3 GSDF troops killed
record.detail: A shell exploded inside the turret of a Western Army Type-10 tank during live-fire training at the Hijudai range around 08:40, killing three and injuring one. The GSDF suspended live-fire training with the same shell type for Type-10 and Type-90 tanks.
record.attribution: Per GSDF statements reported by Stars and Stripes

record.title: ASDF scrambles fall to 595 in FY2025
record.detail: Joint Staff said fighters scrambled 595 times in FY2025 (to March 2026), down from 704, including 366 against Chinese aircraft and 214 against Russian; Chinese drone approaches fell to 16. Officials said activity remains at a high level.
record.attribution: Stars and Stripes citing Japan Joint Staff

record.title: NPA and nine major banks sign pact to trace scam proceeds fast
record.detail: The NPA signed an agreement with nine banks including Mizuho, MUFG, SMBC, Resona and Japan Post Bank, effective June 3, allowing same-day police access to information on accounts receiving scam proceeds instead of multi-week delays.
record.attribution: Jiji Press via Nippon.com citing NPA

record.title: Alleged leader of Poipet-based Japanese fraud ring arrested
record.detail: Aichi prefectural police arrested a 38-year-old man deported from Thailand, alleged leader of a Cambodia (Poipet)-based phone-fraud group with many Japanese members; group losses are put at about ¥1.4 billion, including ¥31.4 million from one Tsukuba victim.
record.attribution: Jiji Press via Nippon.com citing Aichi police

record.title: Tokyo police arrest three linked to Cambodia's Prince Group
record.detail: The MPD arrested three people, including a suspected executive of the Cambodia-based Prince Group fraud network, on suspicion of filing a false residency notification in Chuo Ward in April, reportedly to pursue Japanese permanent residency.
record.attribution: Jiji Press via Nippon.com citing MPD

record.title: Six held over ¥1bn gold smuggled from China in dolls
record.detail: Tokyo MPD arrested six people accused of smuggling 49 kg of gold (about ¥1.075 billion) hidden in life-size dolls declared as mannequins on Jan. 6, evading about ¥107.5 million in consumption tax; delivery was to an Arakawa Ward apartment.
record.attribution: Jiji Press via Nippon.com citing MPD

record.title: China–Russia joint bomber patrol skirts Japan
record.detail: Two Chinese H-6 and two Russian Tu-95 bombers, with Tu-142s and fighters, flew over the East China Sea, Sea of Japan and western Pacific including the Tsushima Strait and south of Amami Oshima; JASDF scrambled from Western Air Defense Command. China called it the 11th joint strategic air patrol.
record.attribution: USNI News citing Japan and South Korea defense ministries and Chinese/Russian statements

record.title: Over 10,000 heatstroke ambulance transports in one week
record.detail: FDMA said 10,857 people were taken to hospital for heatstroke in the week to July 19, 2.4 times the prior week and the first week above 10,000 since tracking began May 1; 14 died and 321 were severe cases.
record.attribution: Figures per FDMA as reported by Jiji Press

record.title: Joint China–Russia naval patrol sails off Hokkaido and Chiba
record.detail: Chinese cruiser Anshan, destroyer Kaifeng and an oiler with Russian corvette Rezkiy operated about 220 km NE of Cape Inubo and 300 km SE of Cape Nosappu on July 25–26, monitored by Japanese forces.
record.attribution: USNI News citing Japan Joint Staff Office

record.title: Record five-day run of 40C readings; 40.8C in Mino
record.detail: Japan logged five straight days with 40C or above through July 25, the longest such streak on record, peaking at 40.8C in Mino, Gifu; 22 locations had reached 40C in 2026 so far. Heatstroke alerts covered 37 of 47 prefectures.
record.attribution: Temperature data per JMA as reported by The Watchers

record.title: Deadly quake strikes Kumamoto; intensity 7 recorded
record.detail: A quake reaching the top intensity 7 on the Japanese scale struck Kumamoto Prefecture; by July 30 the prefecture reported 17 confirmed dead plus six in cardiopulmonary arrest, 59 injured and 10,467 evacuees, with a mall explosion in Kashima and a collapsed mill chimney among deadliest sites.
record.agency: Kumamoto prefectural disaster HQ; Japan Meteorological Agency
record.attribution: Nippon.com citing Kumamoto prefectural disaster response headquarters

record.title: Kumamoto quake death toll climbs to 34
record.detail: The death toll from the magnitude 7.1 quake near Uki rose to 34, nearly half from a Nippon Paper Industries mill collapse and a possible gas explosion at an Aeon store; about 40,000 homes lost power and rail services were halted, per Kumamoto prefecture via Reuters.

record.title: JMA warns of violent winds as Typhoon Chan-hom nears Kanto
record.detail: JMA warned of violent winds, high waves and heavy rain in Kanto and Tohoku coastal areas; at 15:00. Chan-hom (No. 15) was about 130 km east of Mito at 980 hPa, with gusts to 35 m/s.
record.attribution: Forecast and warning issued by JMA, reported by Jiji Press

record.title: Typhoon Chan-hom makes first-ever typhoon landfall in Ibaraki
record.detail: Chan-hom made landfall in Ibaraki around 20:00 while moving unusually from east to west, the first typhoon landfall in the prefecture since records began in 1951, JMA said.
record.attribution: Per JMA as reported by Jiji Press

record.title: Chan-hom leaves 3,000+ homes without power; 60 Haneda flights cut
record.detail: TEPCO Power Grid reported more than 3,000 homes without power in Ibaraki and Tochigi; about 60 flights were cancelled at Haneda and five people had minor injuries. Trains were back to normal by the next morning.
record.attribution: Outage figures per TEPCO Power Grid; AP report

record.title: North Korean ballistic missile lands outside Japan EEZ
record.detail: MOD said at least one ballistic missile launched eastward around 05:59 flew about 690 km at ~90 km altitude and fell in the Sea of Japan outside Japan's EEZ; no damage to ships or aircraft reported.
record.attribution: Defense Minister Koizumi extraordinary press conference

record.title: Record rain floods Chiba; deaths and mass stranding
record.detail: More than 360 mm fell in 24 hours in Chiba Prefecture, flooding about 80 homes; four were confirmed dead with others missing, more than 230,000 people were advised to seek shelter and 4,000 were evacuated from Soga station, per Al Jazeera citing prefectural officials. Over 22,000 households lost power.
record.attribution: Al Jazeera citing Chiba Prefecture disaster management office, JMA and TEPCO

record.title: Tobu Spacia express kills four track workers at Shin-Kanuma
record.detail: A Tokyo-bound Spacia limited express struck a herbicide-spraying crew at Shin-Kanuma Station at 08:29, killing three workers and a supervisor; about 50 passengers were unhurt and service was halted for several hours. Lookout actions are under investigation.
record.attribution: Per AP, citing Tobu Railway and police

record.title: M5.9 quake in southern Ibaraki injures at least 37
record.detail: A magnitude 5.9 quake at about 68 km depth in southern Ibaraki shook Tokyo, Saitama and Chiba, injuring at least 37 people (one seriously) and disrupting Tokyo-area train services; JMA said there was no tsunami concern.
record.agency: Japan Meteorological Agency; Fire and Disaster Management Agency

record.title: Philippines deports four Japanese linked to fraud
record.detail: The Philippine Bureau of Immigration deported four Japanese nationals described as overstaying, undocumented and linked to fraud and theft.
record.attribution: Daily Tribune citing Philippine Bureau of Immigration

record.title: Level 5 emergency flood warning for Shonai River in Nagoya
record.detail: JMA and the land ministry issued the top Level 5 flood warning for the Shonai River system at 18:20, covering 14 municipalities in Aichi and Gifu including Nagoya, Seto, Tajimi and Toki.
record.agency: Japan Meteorological Agency; Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism
record.attribution: Warning issued by JMA and the land ministry

record.title: Heavy rain in Tokai injures 23, floods 90 homes
record.detail: Nagoya's Chikusa Ward had 219.5 mm in 24 hours and Shizuoka's Aoi Ward 267.0 mm; 23 people were slightly hurt, 45 homes flooded above floor level and about 200 vehicles were stranded in Nagoya. The Shonai River Level 5 warning was lifted at 00:40.
record.attribution: Rainfall per JMA; damage figures as reported by Jiji Press

record.title: Internet-enabled fraud losses hit record ¥176bn in H1 2026
record.detail: The NPA said internet-enabled fraud losses rose 45% year on year to ¥176 billion in January–June 2026, and flagged overseas-origin phishing, with China hosting 45% of identified phishing servers.
record.attribution: MLex citing NPA announcement of Sept. 10, 2026

record.title: Gold-bar scam losses reach ¥8.13bn in first half
record.detail: NPA data show scams demanding gold bars cost victims ¥8.13 billion in January–June 2026, above the ¥6.02 billion for all of 2025; about ¥5.3 billion came via police impersonation, and 90% of victims were 60 or older. NPA asked dealers to flag suspicious first-time purchases.
record.attribution: Jiji Press via The Nation citing NPA data

record.title: Thai raid on Bangkok call centre targeting Japanese victims
record.detail: Thai immigration police raided a Bang Bon mansion running fake-Japanese-police call scams, detaining 14–15 people including four Japanese nationals and seizing fake Japanese police uniforms and Japanese-language scripts; the alleged Chinese boss remains at large.
record.attribution: Khaosod English citing Thai immigration police; four Japanese per Real Voice Japan

record.title: Typhoon Dujuan kills at least 4 near Tokyo; 275 flights cut
record.detail: The year's 25th typhoon skirted the Kanto coast, killing at least four people (one in Yokosuka) with six missing; about 45,000 households in Kanagawa lost power and JAL and ANA cancelled 275 flights, with some Tokaido Shinkansen services suspended.
record.attribution: Casualty figures per NHK as reported by Al Jazeera; toll may have risen later
